add.text:
You clean up one chunk of dictated (speech-to-text) text. Stay as close to verbatim as possible.

Fix ONLY:
- obvious typos or mis-hearings, only when you are certain what was meant
- capitalization: a new sentence starts with a capital letter
- punctuation: a question mark only at the end of an actual question; sentence-ending punctuation where a sentence clearly ends
- filler words: remove "um", "uh", "ah", "er", "you know" and "like" used as filler (not as a real comparison), and stutters/repeated words like "the, the"

Never rephrase, reorder, summarize, or change the intent or word choice otherwise.

Number every sentence of your output, in original order: "S1. ", "S2. ", etc., one sentence per line. If you are honestly unsure what a sentence means, still give your best-effort cleaning, but start that line with "S2? " (a question mark instead of a period) and add ", unclear: <a short clarifying question>" right after the sentence text. Output ONLY those numbered lines — no heading, no commentary, nothing else.

Clean this chunk:
I don't know if it needs to be a visible flag, although maybe it could be. Well, I mean, I do think like maybe a visual of what has been read. So like it's you have this highlight feature that kind of highlights the words as they're being read. And so that could just persist. I mean, it's a little bit like, I don't know. The highlight is a little bit, too bold or just, you know, vibrant or whatever. It's having a, more of a subtle playback could, well, maybe we turn the, text kind of muted again and light it up as it's being read . That could be a nice subtle effect. And then when you tap the card itself, it plays and pauses or resumes and/or pauses if currently playing. And then maybe there's like a voice toolbar should be above and or below. Right now, the chat bubbles don't have enough room for that . But basically, as each bubble is being played, you could have... have a little icon appear above or again below. I mean, we have the play button as a very tiny toolbar at the bottom, and I don't mind it. It's nice and compact. However, it's kind of hard to hit that play and pause button. and like tapping on the screen with my right thumb rather than have to like stretch my thumb down to the bottom left corner is probably a good idea. I'm not sure what this little person icon does. Can I click on that? Okay, so I think that turns off the voice mode, which is also interesting. I didn't really test that yet. Maybe I should. There is a rewind 10 seconds. And then what's interesting is the heart, the voice name for the default voice is heart. And it's not bad voice, but I thought maybe the heart, well , the name there just says heart. And it doesn't really look like a dropdown, by the way, and it probably should. well, at least the down chevron that we have on light mode select elements. It looks like it's a default select element based on the pop-up that appears. Anyway, the drop-down isn't present, so it wasn't evident to me it's a drop-down. I thought it was actually like a like button. a like button. Yeah, I thought the heart was, you know, like give a heart to this response or something. So anyway, I clicked it and then it pops up this voice selection mode. So that could be a little better. And then on the little ear slider to the right of that, if you could tell me what that does is that like a threshold for you know, interruption or something.
